indexing.note: IRC 1(f) cost-of-living adjustment, applied as for the federal brackets (N.D.C.C. 57-38-30.3(1)(g))

not_modelled.what: Marriage penalty credit (line 22): joint filers with North Dakota taxable income over 81,036 and a lower qualified income over 47,550 get a worksheet credit of up to 312, figured as a difference of schedule taxes.
Licensed peace officer retirement benefits are excluded in full (line 9) for a retired officer with 20 years of service or retired disabled.
Interest on U.S. obligations (savings bonds, Treasury bills and notes) is subtracted (line 5); a projection does not hold this share of interest.
Military pay on active or reserve duty or in the national guard is subtracted (line 11).
Income of an enrolled tribal member living on a North Dakota reservation, from reservation sources, is subtracted (line 7).
College SAVE contributions are deductible up to 5,000, or 10,000 if married filing jointly (line 12).
Human organ donor expenses up to 10,000 and the 5,241 stillborn child deduction (Schedule ND-1SA lines 6 and 8).
A lump-sum retirement distribution elected onto federal Form 4972 is added back (Schedule ND-1SA line 1).
Credit for income tax paid to another state (line 21, Schedule ND-1CR); the schedule is not in the sources.

approximations.what: The marriage penalty credit is left out.
approximations.size: At most 312 a year, joint returns only. Example: joint taxable income 200,000 and each spouse's qualified income 100,000 gives a credit of 311.51.

approximations.what: The dividend exclusion is applied to all dividends; the booklet allows it only on qualified dividends (Form 1040 line 3a).
approximations.size: At most 1% of non-qualified dividends (40% of them at the 2.5% top rate).

approximations.what: Municipal bond interest is treated as exempt. The booklet prints no rule; this follows the form, which starts from federal taxable income and has no addition line for it.
approximations.size: If North Dakota does tax it, at most 2.5% of the interest.

approximations.what: The long-term gain exclusion is applied to long-term gains; the worksheet uses the smaller of net long-term gain and overall net gain, so a net short-term loss reduces it.
approximations.size: At most 1% of the short-term loss (40% of it at the 2.5% top rate).

approximations.what: Interest on U.S. obligations is not subtracted (not_modelled).
The Schedule ND-1SA addition for a Form 4972 lump-sum distribution is not made (not_modelled).
approximations.size: Only for a filer who elects Form 4972; at most 2.5% of the amount added.

approximations.what: Tax below 100,000 is figured on the exact income; the booklet uses a 50-dollar Tax Table row rounded to whole dollars.
approximations.size: About 1 dollar a year at most.
